disposition_mapping.rationale: The council converged against maximalist's merge of assumption-issuance with target-setting: the function survives as a distinct step, but is restructured so mechanical data-sourcing is agent-drafted while the FP&A manager remains the accountable, named publisher and author of the downside scenario (hitl_designer, finance_domain, accounting_standards). Versioning and an offline-capable distribution channel are added per finance_domain's and emerging_economy's non-negotiables.

Near-unanimous council rejection of maximalist's merge into a continuous assumption/target engine: pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect and accounting_standards all held that target-setting is a discrete governance act requiring its own traceable, separately-owned artefact, distinct from the assumptions feeding it. Retained as a human-only step with decision-support analytics permitted but not decision authority; output labelled provisional per finance_domain's refinement, finalised in T6.

Pragmatist's low-risk merge with ABB-05 (same actor, same deadline window) was accepted across the council, including by finance_domain and emerging_economy once the capex data schema and connectivity concerns were preserved. The function and BU-head ownership survive intact per ABB-R-02; the maximalist proposal to also fold in ABB-04 was rejected because BU heads and cost centre owners are frequently different accountable actors (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect).

Kept structurally separate from T3 per the council's dominant view (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, emerging_economy) that cost-centre/headcount ownership, approval chain and granularity are distinct from BU revenue/capex ownership and must remain separately traceable for accountability during challenge. Agent-assisted baseline drafting is added with mandatory deviation-rationale capture (hitl_designer, emerging_economy), while resisting automated headcount optimisation as the primary mechanism (emerging_economy).

Merged into the unified BU submission step per the pragmatist/finance_domain-endorsed, council-wide-accepted efficiency gain, while the business-case-above-threshold gate is preserved as a hard, rule-based, non-bypassable control (ABB-R-04; agentic_architect, hitl_designer) with a distinct capex schema retained inside the merged step (finance_domain) and central reviewer support for under-resourced submitters (emerging_economy).

The council's strongest consensus: consolidation is restructured around a single, deterministic, reused Consolidation Agent (agentic_architect, accounting_standards) applying the same policy and FX logic across every invocation, with mandatory hard-stop-and-escalate on reconciliation breaks (agentic_architect, hitl_designer), itemised exchange differences (accounting_standards, KB-08), an explicit kickback path to T3/T4 (finance_domain, agentic_architect), versioned run logging to preserve the audit trail under repeated re-consolidation (accounting_standards' conflict-flag), and a documented spreadsheet fallback path for units without reliable system/FX access, built to consume the same versioned policy/FX package (emerging_economy, accounting_standards). KB-06 and KB-07 inputs remain explicit, named and visible per ABB-R-05/ABB-R-07, rejecting any 'black box' automation.

Maximalist's proposal to absorb review-and-challenge into a continuous, self-flagging property of the consolidation engine is rejected: six of seven other members (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, emerging_economy, accounting_standards) independently held that this is a bounded, human-negotiation function that cannot be dissolved into a standing system property, since ABB-R-08's governance gate requires a closed, approvable artefact. The step is restructured, not eliminated: agent-generated briefing packs and repeated re-runs of the Consolidation Agent focus human attention (hitl_designer, agentic_architect), rounds are capped and timeboxed with asynchronous/batched cadence as default (pragmatist, emerging_economy), the downside scenario is actively re-applied as a stress test (finance_domain, agentic_architect), and provisional targets from T2 are finalised here (finance_domain).

Unanimous: board approval is a non-negotiable governance act that no agent may perform or ratify. Strengthened per hitl_designer and agentic_architect's concession so the board pack must surface the downside scenario and material judgment flags unsanitised, preventing approval from becoming ceremonial.

Mechanical load/lock is automated (agentic_architect, maximalist) but the council resolved the attestation-vs-automation conflict in favour of hitl_designer's position: a named, accountable individual must attest that loaded figures equal the board-approved document on every lock event, not merely on mismatch, because a purely self-certifying automated checksum is a weaker evidentiary position than today's manual touch (accounting_standards' concession). The Lock Agent is hard-wired to trigger only after T7 (ABB-R-08), and the displaced manual-loading role is explicitly named as transitioning into the attestor function rather than being silently absorbed (emerging_economy, agentic_architect).

steps.actor: FP&A manager (accountable publisher), supported by Assumptions Drafting Agent
steps.description: An Assumptions Drafting Agent pulls macro feeds (inflation, FX, rates) and generates a template downside-scenario draft from approved external data sources, but the FP&A manager remains the accountable publisher who authors/edits and signs off the final downside macro scenario and the central planning assumptions before release. The package is versioned (v1, v1.1, ...) so submitters can trace which assumption vintage their plan was built on, and is distributed through both a central portal and a downloadable, lockable template bundle so units without reliable continuous connectivity receive the same package on the same terms, not a degraded fallback.
steps.name: Issue calendar and central planning assumptions
outputs: Downside macro scenario (authored, basis-of-judgment note attached)

steps.description: CEO/CFO set top-down revenue, margin and cost targets, informed by the strategic plan and T1's assumptions. Analytics may surface sensitivity tables and prior-year trend data as decision support, but the target itself is a human governance decision, not an agent output with an override option. The targets are issued labelled 'provisional' and are published together with the reasoning and margin/growth drivers behind them, since in practice they are revisited once bottom-up submissions and review (T6) surface conflicting operational reality.
steps.name: Set top-down targets
outputs: Provisional top-down targets with stated reasoning/drivers

steps.actor: Business unit heads, supported by Planning Assistant Agent and a named central FP&A capex reviewer
steps.description: Business unit heads prepare and own a single submission package combining revenue/volume plans and capex requests against one deadline window, replacing today's two separate submission rituals for the same actor. A Planning Assistant Agent pre-populates drafts from historicals, pipeline and driver data; the BU head remains the accountable author and must record a documented rationale wherever the submitted number deviates from the agent's baseline. Capex retains its own distinct schema (asset class, useful life, depreciation timing) rather than flattening into undifferentiated line items, because consolidation needs that shape to drive depreciation, balance-sheet additions and cash-flow timing. A deterministic, rule-based gate blocks submission of any capex line above the published threshold unless a business case is attached; above-threshold cases are paired with a named central FP&A reviewer/coach so the gate is met in substance, not just on a template. Submission supports an offline-capable, periodically-synced template format as a first-class channel, not a workaround.
inputs: Provisional top-down targets with stated reasoning/drivers
Business case for capex above threshold
Operational driver data and prior actuals
steps.name: Integrated business unit submission: revenue, volume and capex

steps.actor: Cost centre owners, supported by baseline-drafting automation
steps.description: Cost centre owners prepare and own cost centre and headcount budgets, kept as a structurally distinct step from T3 because the actor, approval chain and downstream consumers (payroll systems vs. revenue reporting) differ. Formulaic/fixed-cost rollovers can be automated as a drafting baseline, but headcount and discretionary-spend decisions remain the owner's judgment; any deviation from or acceptance of the automated baseline must carry a recorded rationale so the owner's engagement with the number is auditable, not a passive click. Automated headcount-optimisation models are decision support only and may not become the primary mechanism, preserving local labour-market and informal-economy judgment that a central model cannot see.
inputs: Provisional top-down targets with stated reasoning/drivers
steps.name: Cost centre and headcount budgets

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (accountable reviewer), supported by a single reused Consolidation Agent
steps.description: A single, version-controlled Consolidation Agent performs the mechanical roll-up of T3/T4 submissions, applies the central FX assumptions and the same accounting policies used for actuals, and reconciles P&L, balance sheet and cash flow. FX translation and policy application are deterministic, rule-based and auditable, not generative inference, and the same logic path is reused (not re-implemented) across this step and every iteration inside T6, preventing policy/FX drift between rounds. Exchange differences are preserved as explicit, itemised lines, never netted invisibly. The reconciled three-statement output is surfaced by default, not only on exception; reconciliation breaks, unmapped inputs or FX/policy anomalies hard-stop and route back to the originating T3/T4 submission(s) for correction rather than being silently resolved. Each consolidation run is versioned and logged (inputs, assumption vintage, agent/logic version, timestamp) so any number the board later sees can be traced to a specific run. A documented, equally-valid spreadsheet-based consolidation path exists for units without reliable system/FX-feed access, built to consume the same versioned central policy/FX package so it is reconcilable against, not divergent from, the primary agent's logic. The FP&A analyst remains the accountable reviewer of consolidation output, certifying exceptions and the final reconciled statement.
steps.name: Consolidate into draft three-statement budget
outputs: Draft three-statement budget (reconciled, with itemised exchange differences)

steps.actor: FP&A manager / CFO, with submitters, supported by Variance/Scenario Agent
steps.description: The draft budget is reviewed and challenged in a discrete, bounded negotiation between the FP&A manager/CFO and submitters, which also finalises the provisional targets issued in T2. This step remains irreducibly human: a Variance/Scenario Agent generates briefing packs, re-runs T5's Consolidation Agent against revised submissions, and re-applies the downside macro scenario as a stress test on the draft budget each round, but challenge, trade-off and revision decisions stay with people. Iterations are capped (e.g. two structured rounds) and timeboxed against the T1 calendar, with asynchronous/batched written commentary as the default-supported cadence and live sessions as an enhancement rather than a precondition, so the step does not assume continuous connectivity or infinite availability of scarce senior FP&A/CFO time. The step concludes in a bounded, closed artefact ('the budget as finally challenged and settled') that the board can approve; a continuous variance-flagging property is an input to this step, not a substitute for it.
inputs: Provisional top-down targets with stated reasoning/drivers
steps.name: Review and challenge iterations

steps.description: The board approves the budget. An agent may assemble the board pack, but the approval action and authority remain exclusively with the board. The pack must explicitly carry the downside macro scenario and the material judgment calls/exception flags surfaced during T6, unsanitised, so approval is a substantive act of interrogation rather than a ceremonial sign-off on a document nobody can meaningfully challenge.
inputs: Downside macro scenario and material judgment flags (unsanitised)
steps.name: Board approval

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (named attestor), supported by Lock Agent
steps.description: A Lock Agent is hard-wired to trigger only on receipt of the board-approved artefact from T7, with no path for an earlier or parallel load, and loads the approved figures into the planning system. Before the lock is sealed, a named, accountable individual (successor to the former manual-loading role, explicitly named in the transition plan rather than having the function silently absorbed) attests, on every lock event including clean ones, that the loaded/locked figures are identical to the board-approved document; a validation mismatch halts the lock and escalates rather than proceeding silently or partially. The locked version is the single version used by variance analysis; any post-lock correction must go through a formal, logged, CFO-authorised re-open procedure, never an informal system edit. Units without tier-one EPM licensing retain a documented manual-lock fallback (access-controlled file/version control) carrying the same attestation discipline.
steps.name: Load and lock approved version
